name: YOG'TZE case (word written by Guenther Stoll shortly before his death)
language_candidates: unknown -- 'there seems to be no language in the world that knows this word' per Schmeh
ciphertext_source: Cipherbrain post 21 (Schmeh 2017, sources/schmeh/posts/21-yogtze.txt), fetched 25 Sept 2026, read in full. The word itself, not an image of it, is the primary datum here: Stoll wrote it on paper, shouted 'Jetzt geht mir ein Licht auf!' ('Now I've got it!'), then immediately crossed it out. An image exists (files/2015/09/YOGTZE-Lego-1.png, a LEGO reconstruction of the scene from the 1985 TV show, not a photograph of the original paper) but is not the ciphertext itself.
alphabet: 6 Latin letters (Y O G T Z E) plus one apostrophe, no repeats among the 6 letters

constraints.unicity_note: per UNSOLVED-SURVEY.md row 26, 'below any unicity' -- at N=6 no statistical cryptanalysis of any kind can meaningfully distinguish a real key from chance; this item is a crib-search / lexical-association problem, not a cryptanalytic one
constraints.context: Stoll, a German food engineer, had spoken of paranoid fears about unnamed people ('them') the evening before; hours later he was found severely injured near a crashed car about 100km from home, told witnesses of 'four men' with him, and died en route to hospital; police concluded he had been run over elsewhere while naked and then placed in the car -- a probable murder made to look like an accident, per the case's fame, though Schmeh's own stated view is 'an accident a lot more likely'
constraints.hypotheses_in_source: (1) read with G as '6': 'YO6'TZE', a Romanian radio call sign (unverified); (2) the apostrophe matches Dutch licence-plate formatting; (3) read upside-down/mirrored: roughly '3ZL,90X' (no meaning proposed); (4) 'TZE' as an artificial-flavouring abbreviation used in yoghurt production ('YOG'), tying it to Stoll's own profession (food engineering); (5) an acrostic, the initials of six words. None confirmed; Schmeh lists these as 'many more possible explanations' without endorsing any.
constraints.no_known_language: Schmeh's own summary line: no language is known to contain this word as written

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Acrostic/initialism search: treat Y-O-G-T-Z-E as the initials of a 6-word German (and, as a control comparison, English) phrase Stoll might have blurted after 'now I've got it' -- search common German idioms/warning phrases with this initial pattern via a wordlist-based initials search (tools/judge_plaintext.py's initials_regex mechanism is built for exactly this). Cost $1, Sonnet.

2. Direct lexical/abbreviation search (grep, not cryptanalysis) for 'YOGTZE'/'YOG TZE'/'YOG'TZE' as a period (pre-1984) call sign, product code, chemical/flavouring abbreviation, or file/serial number, across the food-engineering and radio-callsign leads named in the source (hypotheses 1 and 4 above) using open bibliographic search (OpenAlex, Google Books) rather than assuming either is right. Cost $1.

3. Anagram enumeration of the 6 letters (720 permutations, small enough to brute-force) against German and English short-word/phrase lists, since an anagram is at least as plausible a priori as a substitution cipher at N=6. Cost under $1.
matched_control: not applicable at this N -- CLAUDE.md rule 3's matched-control requirement is for cryptanalytic negatives; at N=6 ('below any unicity' per the survey row) no solver-vs-control comparison is meaningful, so none of the three tests above are cryptanalytic in that sense (they are lexical/crib searches, reported as hit/no-hit, not scored against a control); test 1 as actually run (LANE B3 brief, 25 Sept 2026) does use a control in a different, non-cryptanalytic sense -- a wordlist-feasibility comparison against random letter-strings, not a solver-vs-control cryptanalytic gate

cheap_test_done.method: Initials/acrostic feasibility: for the 6 letters Y-O-G-T-Z-E, the minimum across the six positions of (count of distinct wordlist entries starting with that letter) -- the acrostic's bottleneck letter -- computed once for German (tools/data/de20, 42,047 distinct words) and once for English (tools/data/pg1661_holmes.txt + pg2701_mobydick.txt, 19,547 distinct words). No phrase assembled or proposed; hit/no-hit only. Script and full output: specs/cheap-tests/yogtze-1984/{test1_initials.py,test1_output.json,README.md}.

control.draw: 6-letter strings sampled (with replacement) from the same wordlist's own first-letter frequency distribution, same min-count statistic

cheap_test_done.verdict: no-hit -- in both languages the target's own bottleneck-letter count sits below the entire 20-draw control range (percentile 0.0), i.e. YOGTZE is markedly harder to complete as a six-word acrostic than a same-length random letter-string would be, in both German and English general prose. Not evidence for the acrostic hypothesis; a small piece of support for Schmeh's own 'no language knows this word' extended to acrostic initials. No candidate phrase reported.

judge.note: language deliberately omitted (schema_note): N=6 is far below any n-gram language model's useful floor, and the source states no known language contains this word as written -- a judge PASS/FAIL on language here would be noise, not signal

value: low: extensively investigated for four decades by amateurs and at least one TV crime show with no result; N=6 puts this below what any of this repository's cryptanalytic tools can usefully test, so value here is entirely in the cheap lexical/crib searches (test 1-3), not a cryptanalytic campaign
status_25_Sept_2026: open; below any unicity per UNSOLVED-SURVEY.md row 26, consistent with this pass's read of the source (Schmeh: 'the meaning of YOG'TZE... remain[s] a mystery')
schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run goes under cheap_test_done, reported hit/no-hit (no control applies at this N, see matched_control). judge block's language is deliberately left out: N=6 is uninformative for any n-gram-based check, and letters_min=letters_max=6 makes the length check trivially true for any 6-letter candidate -- this judge block mainly documents that a language gate cannot do useful work here, not that one has been wired.
